english.title: Fail to comply with requirement to produce document / information - Private Security Industry Act 2001
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed without reasonable excuse to comply with a requirement imposed by section 19(2) of the Private Security Industry Act 2001 to produce documents or information relating to any matter connected with

(A)_[licensable conduct in which you have been or may be engaged]_
(B)_[the provision by you of security industry services]_
(C)_[matters in respect of which conditions were imposed on you by virtue of a licence or of an approval granted in accordance with arrangements under section 15 of the Act]_

to **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), a person duly authorised in writing by the Private Security Industry Authority for that purpose
english.legislation: Contrary to section 19(5)(b) and (7) of the Private Security Industry Act 2001.

english.standardstatementoffacts:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant failed without reasonable excuse to comply with a requirement imposed by section 19(2) of the Private Security Industry Act 2001 to produce documents or information relating to any matter connected with

(A)_[licensable conduct in which he had been or may have been engaged]_
(B)_[licensable conduct in which she had been or may have been engaged]_
(C)_[the provision by him of security industry services]_
(D)_[the provision by her of security industry services]_
(E)_[matters in respect of which conditions were imposed on him by virtue of a licence or of an approval granted in accordance with arrangements under section 15 of the Act]_
(F)_[matters in respect of which conditions were imposed on her by virtue of a licence or of an approval granted in accordance with arrangements under section 15 of the Act]_

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale

Time limit for prosecutions:
Six months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
